newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks sweep to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks sweep to higher close.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa closed higher Friday in hefty turnover fuelled by a flurry of corporate activity involving blue-chip stocks, dealers said.

"Through all these mergers and acquisitions local companies are obtaining major international financial backing and gaining a competitive advantage," said Luis Corsiglia of brokers Corsiglia y Cia. "This a time of great opportunity and there will be a lot of porfolio shuffling."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV rose 1.4 percent to 778.08 while floor volume swelled to 40.2 million pesos from 24.1 million Thursday.
Over-the-counter turnover surged to 171.5 million pesos from 125.5 million Thursday.
The MerVal closed up 1.4 percent on the week and 1.7 percent higher in May, setting a new five-year high.

"The market as a whole is rubbing up against technical resistance and may not push much higher near-term, but individual stocks like Comercial del Plata have room to stretch, perhaps to all-time highs," Corsiglia said.
Comercial del Plata said Friday it hoped to raise $330 million from deals to sell interests in various undertakings to six Argentine companies.

Also Friday HSBC Holdings said it was buying out the local financial services group Roberts for between $600 and $688 millon, while Spain's Repsol said it would buy stakes in local firms through its subsidiary Astra worth $345 million.

Earlier in the week Spain's Banco Santander announced the purchase of a controlling stake in Banco Rio de la Plata while Banco Frances, controlled by the Spanish Bilbao Vizcaya, recently purchased Banco de Credito Argentino.
"We've never seen so many major corporate deals in such a short period of time -- in the market today obviously the banks were the stars," another trader said.
The bolsa's four listed banks -- Bansud, Banco del Suquia, Banco de Galicia and Banco Frances -- closed up 4.7 percent, 4.6 percent, 3.8 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively.
Other top main-tier gainers were textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, up 2.7 percent, and oil giant YPF, up 1.7 percent.
The only MerVal losers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa and holding company Garovaglio, off 8.0 percent and 0.6 percent, respectively.
The broad market index closed up 1.3 percent, with winners battering losers 50 to nine and 26 issues closing flat.
